title: Lesson 5: Suffering and Trials
description: When life gets hard, God is with you in the valley. Through Joseph's story and James 1:2-4, this lesson shows how God uses trials to grow steadfast faith, and why your pain is never wasted in His hands.

blocks.text: In the last lesson, you began to notice the gifts Jesus has placed in you. Those gifts get used in a broken world, and sooner or later every believer walks through a hard season. This lesson is about suffering: what God is doing in it, and who is with you when it comes.

blocks.title: The Pit, the Prison, and the Palace
blocks.text:
Joseph was seventeen, his father's favorite son, and his older brothers hated him for it. They tore off the special robe his father had given him, threw him into an empty pit, and sold him to traders headed for Egypt. Then they let their father believe Joseph was dead.

In Egypt, Joseph became a slave in the house of Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh. He served faithfully and refused the advances of Potiphar's wife, so she lied about him. Joseph was thrown into prison for something he did not do. Even there, the Bible says, "the LORD was with Joseph and showed him steadfast love" (Genesis 39:21). He explained a dream for Pharaoh's cupbearer and asked only to be remembered. The cupbearer forgot him for two whole years.

Then Pharaoh had dreams no one could explain, and the cupbearer finally remembered. Joseph went from the prison to the palace in a single day and was put in charge of storing grain before seven years of famine. When the famine came, his brothers traveled to Egypt for food and bowed before the brother they had sold, without knowing who he was.

More than twenty years after the pit, Joseph wept and told them who he was. "Do not be distressed or angry with yourselves because you sold me here, for God sent me before you to preserve life" (Genesis 45:5). Years later, when his brothers feared he would finally pay them back, Joseph said, "As for you, you meant evil against me, but God meant it for good, to bring it about that many people should be kept alive, as they are today" (Genesis 50:20).
Joseph's story is not mainly about a strong man. It is about a faithful God who was with Joseph in the pit, in the prison, and in the palace, working the whole time in ways Joseph could not see.
5.1 - What is the hardest season you are walking through right now, or have walked through in the last few years?
The Question Nobody Wants to Ask

If God is good, and if God is powerful, and if He loves His children, then why does life hurt so much sometimes? That question has been asked in every century by every kind of person. It is not a sign of weak faith. It is a sign of paying attention. The Bible does not avoid it, and God is not offended when you ask it.
God Meant It for Good

Look closely at what Joseph said to his brothers. He did not pretend the evil was not evil. You meant evil against me. His brothers chose their cruelty, and they were responsible for it. But Joseph also said, God sent me (Genesis 45:5-8), and God meant it for good.

One event, two intentions. The brothers meant it for harm. God, who rules over all things, meant it for good, and His purpose stood. God was not the author of their sin, and He was never surprised by it. He was sovereign over it, and He wove even their evil into His plan to keep many people alive, including the very brothers who sold Joseph.
And we know that for those who love God all things work together for good, for those who are called according to his purpose.

Paul does not say all things are good. Cancer is not good. Betrayal is not good. He says God works all things together for good for His children. You may not see that good for years. Joseph waited more than twenty, and some of it you will not see until eternity.

A word of care. If someone has abused or deeply wounded you, Joseph's words do not mean that what they did was acceptable, that you must stay in danger, or that you have to call it good. Joseph called evil what it was, and so can you. If you are not safe, tell a pastor or a trusted friend and get help today. God does not ask you to pretend. He comes close.
The LORD is near to the brokenhearted and saves the crushed in spirit.
5.2 - When you read "God meant it for good," what is your first honest response: hope, resistance, or something else?
Trials Produce Steadfastness
Joseph's road ran through a valley before it reached the palace. James, the brother of Jesus, wrote to believers walking that same kind of road.

Count it all joy, my brothers, when you meet trials of various kinds, for you know that the testing of your faith produces steadfastness. And let steadfastness have its full effect, that you may be perfect and complete, lacking in nothing.

James does not say to be happy about suffering. He says to count it joy, a deliberate decision made in the middle of something painful. The decision rests on what you know, not on what you feel. You know the testing is producing something. You know God does not waste pain. Paul says it another way: suffering produces endurance, endurance produces character, and character produces hope (Romans 5:3-4). Walk the road James describes, one step at a time.
5.3 - Looking back on a hard season, what did God grow in you that might not have grown any other way?
God Is With You in the Valley

One of the most important things the Bible says about suffering is not why it happens but who is there when it does. Psalm 23 does not promise a path that avoids the valley of the shadow of death. It says, "Even though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil, for you are with me."

Jesus walked into the darkest valley of all. On the cross He cried out, "My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?" (Matthew 27:46), so that you would never be forsaken. Three days later He walked out of the grave. That is the ground of your hope. If God did not spare His own Son for you, He will not abandon you in your valley (Romans 8:32). Because of the cross and the empty tomb, the worst thing is never the last thing.

And God never comforts you for you alone. He "comforts us in all our affliction, so that we may be able to comfort those who are in any affliction" (2 Corinthians 1:4). Your valley may prepare you to sit with a hurting friend and say, God was faithful in my darkness. He will be faithful in yours.
5.4 - Who in your life is walking through a hard season, and how could you walk alongside them this week?
Bitter or Better?

Every season of suffering takes you in one direction or the other. It makes you harder and more cynical about God and people, or it makes you more tender, more trusting, and more aware of your need and other people's.

The key choice is where you take your honest pain. If you bring your raw, unanswered questions to God the way David did in the Psalms, the pain gets processed in His presence, and the result is often deeper faith. If you nurse it privately and let it become a case against Him, the result is bitterness. The Psalms of lament are not the prayers of people who gave up on God. They are the prayers of people who refuse to take their pain anywhere else.
Why are you cast down, O my soul, and why are you in turmoil within me? Hope in God; for I shall again praise him, my salvation and my God.
5.5 - What is one honest thing you need to bring to God right now that you have been carrying quietly?
This Week's Practice

This week, pray one of the lament Psalms out loud: Psalm 13, 42, or 88. Read it slowly, and notice how the writer moves from raw pain to remembered truth, and often to renewed hope. Even Psalm 88, which ends in the dark, is still a prayer. Bring it honest, anchor it in what you know, and wait for hope to rise. You do not have to fix the feeling. You just have to bring it to the right Person.

Then write down one hard thing you are carrying. Beneath it, write: The LORD is near to the brokenhearted. If you can, add: God can bring good even from this. Not because you feel it yet, and never to call evil good, but as an act of trust in the God who walked with Joseph to the last chapter.
Lesson 5 Review

Suffering is real, and the Bible does not hide from it. Joseph's brothers meant evil, and God meant it for good, without ever being the author of their sin. Trials test your faith, and tested faith grows steadfast and complete. Jesus walked the deepest valley to the cross and rose again, so you never walk yours alone. God is with you in the valley, and He never wastes your pain. So bring your pain to Him, not away from Him.
In the next lesson, you will meet two men who sang in a prison at midnight, and see why worship is the natural response to who God is.
